classification.difficultyReason: Identify all six triangles and compare their areas using their common perpendicular height and different base lengths.

content.prompt: Find all 6 triangles in this figure and rank them by area.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 11 figure at the bottom of printed page 270
spec.description: Unshaded triangle ABE with collinear baseline points B, C, D, E, internal segments AC and AD, two supplied segment lengths and a full-base double-headed dimension arrow. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: BC = 3.5 cm, CD = 3.5 cm and BE = 10.5 cm. DE has no supplied label. All six triangles share apex A and have bases on BE. Coordinates reproduce the diagram arrangement without supplying a height.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no inferred DE length, height or ranking is printed.

inlines.text: All six triangles have the same perpendicular height, so their areas are proportional to their base lengths.

answer.worked:
Each triangle uses apex $A$ and two of the points $B,C,D,E$, giving the six triangles $ABC$, $ABD$, $ABE$, $ACD$, $ACE$ and $ADE$.
$$\begin{align*}DE&=10.5-3.5-3.5\\DE&=3.5\text{ cm}\\BD&=3.5+3.5\\BD&=7\text{ cm}\\CE&=3.5+3.5\\CE&=7\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
All six triangles have the same perpendicular height from $A$ to the line $BE$. Since $\text{area}=\tfrac12\times\text{base}\times\text{height}$, compare their base lengths: $BC=CD=DE=3.5\text{ cm}$, $BD=CE=7\text{ cm}$ and $BE=10.5\text{ cm}$.
Thus, from smallest to largest area, $ABC=ACD=ADE$, then $ABD=ACE$, then $ABE$. Their area groups are in the ratio $1:2:3$.
